_doc: THE SHEET PINS — the ONE pinned identity of the owner's injury/sitter annotation. The engine asserts these three facts about docs/owner_annotations/SITTER_2026_v1.csv BEFORE it reads a row of it: md5, row count, injured=Y count. Any of them failing HALTS the build, loudly, fail-closed — that is unchanged and it is the whole point of the file. What changed (PLAN_v6 PACKAGE 3a, 2026-08-21) is WHERE the three facts live: they were SIX LITERALS IN TWO DUPLICATED IN-ENGINE BLOCKS (O41_INJ_MD5/O41_INJ_ROWS/O41_INJ_Y at ORDER 41 and _SHEET_MD5/_SHEET_ROWS/_SHEET_Y at ORDER 42 in engine/rl_after/_merged_recover.py), which made every sheet update an ENGINE EDIT and let the two copies drift. Erratum E4 of the R23 runbook is the record of what that cost: a re-cut that moved only the ORDER 42 trio dies at ORDER 41 with the sheet already changed. There is now ONE declaration — this file — and both blocks read it.
_the_guards_are_UNCHANGED: Moving the values moved no guard. ORDER 41 still reads the pins only under RL_O41_INJ, ORDER 42 still reads them only inside _o42_state under RL_O42, ORDER 41 still HALTS FIRST, and every halt message is byte-unchanged. A dial-off build reads this file not at all, exactly as it read the literals not at all before. An ABSENT or MALFORMED pin file HALTS every build that would have read the pins (SHEET-PIN HALT), because the alternative is a build that prices an owner input nobody pinned.
_writer_of_record: SOLE WRITER, as of 2026-08-21: `tools/land round` (PLAN_v6 PACKAGE 2b, tools/landing/steps.py -> steps.sheet). 2b landed, so the interim arrangement this line used to describe has ENDED: the manual path in docs/runbooks/R23_RUNBOOK.md §4 H2 was the writer for the 3a->2b window only, and it is now the DOCUMENTED FALLBACK — kept because an unexercised fallback is fake safety (PLAN_v6 2a.3), retired for this act type on the owner's word and not before (2a.4). THE RULE BINDS THE PINNED FACTS — sheet_md5, sheet_rows, sheet_injured_y, and the pinned_at/provenance that record when and why they moved. Nothing else may move them: not a seat by hand, not a build, not a repair. THIS HEADER IS THE RULE'S DURABLE HOME — the runbook repeats it, and a runbook is a procedure, not a law's home (the R23 runbook needed five errata inside one round, and a sixth to say the pins had left the engine). The `_doc` keys themselves are prose, amended by the act that changes the rule; this act is that act.
_manifest_checked: THE THREE PINNED FACTS ARE MANIFEST-CHECKED CARRIER FIELDS as of 2026-08-21 — release_manifest_check.py identities `sheet` / `sheet_rows` / `sheet_injured_y`, carrier group `sheet_pins`, one field each (43 carrier fields across 11 identities and 8 files). PACKAGE 3a specified this and deferred it to 2b in its own words: 'the sheet md5 + the pin file become MANIFEST-CHECKED CARRIER FIELDS with the round lander as sole writer once 2b lands'. TRUTH IS COMPUTED FROM THE SHEET, never typed: the gate reads the file THIS declaration names, md5s the raw bytes, counts csv.DictReader rows and injured=Y rows — character for character what ORDER 41 and ORDER 42 do — and asserts these three fields agree. So a sheet that moves without its declaration moving is now caught by a gate BEFORE it halts a build, and it is caught in the acceptance runner's first check, where the blocked-once law reports it exactly once.
_review_forcing_step: A SHEET CHANGE IS A DATA COMMIT, NOT AN ENGINE EDIT — and it still owes a review-forcing step. PREREG-LITE, committed WITH the data change, in the same commit as the sheet and this file: the PREDICTED sheet md5, the PREDICTED row count and injured=Y count, and the DISCLOSED MOVERS the re-cut is expected to produce. Predicted first, measured after; a prereg-lite is corrected against the tree, never the tree against the prereg-lite (process law P9's shape, at data scale).
provenance: Values last MOVED by the FW1 injury-sheet re-cut of 2026-08-30, on the owner's word: "Yes, Viney has returned. Nobody else." jack-viney flipped injured Y->N because he played in Finals Week 1 (Melbourne, SC 55) while the pinned sheet still carried him injured=Y / out until 2027. ORDER 42 caught the contradiction at the catchup_preflight door and refused the advance — correctly: applying FW1 would have incremented his games_2026 while the sheet said he had none and would get none, and the board regen would then have halted INSIDE the staged transaction. injured=Y 35 -> 34, rows unchanged at 219, md5 21361291f26d35108b88f92f885c5063 -> 61ef3e61a685909784c1d6eb23859788. EXACTLY ONE ROW DIFFERS, asserted field-by-field before the write: only `injured` moved on only Jack Viney. The previous re-cut was R23's of 2026-08-20 (harry-armstrong and judson-clarke, Y->N, 37 -> 35), on the owner's word "All good on the injury sheet. Fine by me."
